newsitem.title: HONG KONG: MARKET VIEW - Asia markets seen firm on U.S. rally.
newsitem.headline: MARKET VIEW - Asia markets seen firm on U.S. rally.

text.p: Asian stocks are expected to gain ground in the coming week, although Tokyo shares will continue to come under pressure.
Steady jobs data in the United States combined with last week's decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged lifted the Dow Industrials on Friday.
The Dow Industrials gained 82.74 points on Friday to close at 6,855.80 while the U.S. 30-year benchmark bond ended 23/32 stronger to yield 6.70 percent.
Dealers said the strong U.S. performance could reinvigorate many Asian stock markets following last week's intermittent closures for public holidays such as Chinese New Year.

Hong Kong is one market expected to gain from the U.S. rally following a 2.54 percent jump last week. The Hang Seng index closed at 13,660.50 on Wednesday ahead of the Lunar New Year holiday on Thursday and Friday.
But in Tokyo, weakness in banking stocks and a close below 18,000 in the Nikkei 225 index could weigh on stocks in the coming week.
Among the smaller Asian bourses, Manila and Jakarta are expected to outperform with foreign investors retaining a bullish outlook for both economies.
But Thailand is a source of growing concern following last week's five-percent slide to 747.76.
HONG KONG - The stable interest rate outlook is expected to buoy the Hang Seng index to 14,000 points in the coming week, with analysts expecting the blue chip barometer to hit new records soon.

"Investors are expected to return from the Chinese New Year holiday in a buying mood. I am sure Hong Kong will set a new record in the short term," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
The Hang Seng index rose 112.07 points to close at 13,660.50 on Wednesday ahead of the Chinese New Year holiday.
Rossiter said the downside was limited at 13,600 points this coming week and profit-takers were likely to emerge around 14,000 points.
The intra-day record high for the blue chip index stands at 14,004.93 points, hit on January 16 this year.
TOKYO - Volatile trade is expected next week in Tokyo stocks, which will see-saw between buying of blue chips and selling of bank and construction shares, brokers said.
"Distrust in the construction and bank sectors were renewed as rumours of financial woes at Nippon Credit Bank and Tobishima Corp dragged the market under with them," a trader said.
The 225-share Nikkei average shed 2.6 percent, finishing at 17,867.04 on January 7.
Brokers added that a close below the 18,000 level for the first time in over a week could drag stocks lower again soon.
"If profit-taking of the high-flying blue chips sets in on top of the weakness in domestic sector shares, the losses could be pretty hefty," said Keiko Kondo, a strategist at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc.
Market sources see a floor at the recent closing low of 17,300 with potential gains capped at 18,300.
Markets are closed in Tokyo on Tuesday for the National Foundation Day holiday.
KUALA LUMPUR - Dealers say the market could resume with an upward bias next Wednesday, partly on the U.S. markets rally.
"I think it will be a good, high volume week," said Tony Shue, a vice president in institutional sales at Jupiter Securities. "People will have to make up for the lost volume."
An institutional dealer said the Second Board should see continued selective interest.
The small-capitalisation index has been outpacing the Composite Index of blue chips, with some analysts expecting it to get back to the 650 to 660 level over the short-term.
Last week, the benchmark Composite Index closed 25.23 points, or 2.07 percent, higher at 1,241.95 on Wednesday against a close of 1216.72 on January 31.
The Kuala Lumpur share market will be closed until Tuesday for the Chinese New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr festivals.
TAIPEI - Taiwan share prices were likely to continue to firm when trading resumes on February 11 after the seven-day lunar new year holiday, analysts said.

Brokers said the central bank was unlikely to take steps to tighten liquidity following Wednesday's announcement that the consumer price index for January was just 1.96 percent -- well below the expectations of economists and even the central bank.
"Such a low CPI growth should ensure the central bank keeps its stable-to-loose monetary policy," said Nomura Securities analyst Ben Lee.
On Monday, the index ended up 31.49 points or 0.43 percent at 7,346.88. Monday's close was up 0.88 percent from 7,283.40 last Friday.
A 7,300-7,500 range was seen for next week.
BANGKOK - Thai stocks are expected to extend losses next week as currency jitters and continued high interest rates undermine the battered market, traders said.
The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index shed 5.11 percent over the week to end near a 4-1/2 year low on Friday of 747.76, compared to 788.04 a week earlier.
"We think the currency issue will continue to worry the market next week," said a trader at TISCO.

The Thai baht has come under speculative attack recently following balance of payments shortfalls in November and December. Continued high interest rates to defend the baht coupled with high short term rates running at six-month highs of 25-28 percent will also add to selling pressure, analysts said.
"The issue of high overnight interest rates is likely to dampen sentiment," said Youseef Abboud, an investment analyst at Wall Street Finance and Securities.
JAKARTA - Jakarta share prices are expected to remain steady in the coming week, but trading is seen slow due to Eid al-Fitr Moslem celebrations, brokers said.
"The underlying tone is very, very strong. It may go up after the market re-opens next Wednesday," a foreign broker with a European securities house said.
On Friday, the Jakarta composite index closed at 7.42 points or 1.07 percent higher at 694.28 points against last's week close of 691.12 points.
The Jakarta stock exchange will be closed until February 11 due to the Eid al-Fitr Moslem celebrations and will resume trading on Wednesday.

SINGAPORE - Dealers in Singapore said they expected activity to pick up the pace on Tuesday after Friday's Lunar New Year and Monday's Eid holidays, but said long term predictions were harder to make.
"Singapore is very short-term these days," said one dealer.
Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials Index ended at 2,203.39 on Thursday, 13.08 points or 0.06 percent lower from the previous Friday's 2,216.47. - - - -
WELLINGTON - New Zealand shares and market leader Telecom in particular were savaged this week and brokers said there was little on the short-term horizon to effect a change in sentiment.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended at 2,328.29, 58.45 points or 2.45 percent lower than its 2,386.74 close last Friday.
"I think we've got to see particularly the (90-day) bank bill rate come off significantly before we'll get a resumption in life here," said Cavill White's Don Turkington.
